title: Breastfeeding consultation
what: A specialist helps you get breastfeeding going. They show you how to latch your baby well and work through your difficulties.
why: For sore or cracked nipples, engorged breasts, low milk supply, or if your baby is not gaining weight well.
duration: the consultation usually takes 1 to 1.5 hours
tell_doctor: How often and how long your baby feeds
How many wet diapers a day
Pain, cracks, or lumps in the breast
Your baby's weight at birth and now

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: It helps to come when your baby will soon be hungry, so the specialist can watch a feed.

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: For 1 to 2 days, write down when your baby fed and how many diapers there were.

bring: Your breast pump or bottle, if you use one
steps: The specialist asks about the birth and feeding
Your breasts and nipples are checked
Your baby's mouth and sucking are checked
Comfortable positions and a good latch are shown
A plan is made: how often to feed and what to do next
feel: If your breasts hurt, the check may feel tender
after: Try the positions and latch you were shown
Keep track of wet diapers and your baby's weight
A follow-up visit or call in a few days is often needed
red_flags: The breast is red, hot, and painful, with a fever over 38°C (100.4°F): see a doctor
Your baby is floppy, has few wet diapers, or will not feed well: see a pediatrician urgently

faq.q: How do I know my baby is getting enough milk?
faq.a: Usually enough if there are plenty of wet diapers and your baby is gaining weight. The pediatrician will check.
No. Strong pain is often from a poor latch. It can be fixed.

faq.q: Can I breastfeed if I take medicines?
faq.a: Often yes. Tell your doctor what you take, and they will decide.

reminders.text: Breastfeeding consultation soon. Bring your baby and your feeding notes. Best to come when your baby will soon be hungry.
